trap-superlative.notes: RECOMPUTED. (a) '76x improves on the proton-fitted single-E_0 assembly (14.7% mean)': 14.7 / 0.18406 = 79.86x, not 76x — the sentence's own two figures are mutually inconsistent by 5%, and 76x would require the old mean to be 13.99% or the new to be 0.1934%. (b) 'This MATCHES the standalone ... formula's empirical fit (0.13-0.16% mean across the same spectrum)': 0.184% lies OUTSIDE [0.13, 0.16], so the per-derivation assembly is 15% to 42% WORSE than the fit it is compared with; PROPOSED wording, 'is within a factor 1.2 to 1.4 of'. (c) The headline 'Mean = 0.184%' is right — I recomputed all twelve error rows and the mean from the table and every figure matches — but it averages in the p and n rows, which are 0.000 BY CONSTRUCTION as the free-particle baseline; over the 10 genuinely predicted rows the mean is 0.2209%. (d) alpha = m_e x 8G = 3.74446989 MeV is high by 2.73 ppm against its own definition: recomputed at 25 dps with CODATA m_e = 0.51099895069 and 8G = 7.327724753417752, m_e x 8G = 3.744459660. Catalan itself is handled CORRECTLY here (G approx 0.9160), unlike the s4-s3 proof block in this batch. (e) 'The total B(Z,N) ... is positive for bound systems. QED' asserts positivity without deriving it, under a QED box.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: Three sweep-damage sites leave broken syntax: 'implemented in / the formal derivation / as assemble_per_derivation_weights(Z, N)' (a script name replaced by the placeholder phrase); 'per / the *atomic-braid mass formula* in the Particles chapter, the binding correction is ...'; and 'This matches the standalone the *atomic-braid mass formula* in the Particles chapter formula's empirical fit', which stacks two determiners and two nouns and does not parse.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: NOT FIXED INLINE because repairing them requires the original script name and link text, which the substitution destroyed. Measured spread of this class: the phrase 'the formal derivation' occurs 38 times across 27 .md files in mass-theory alone, and 'the canonical formalism' appears in 56 files corpus-wide. SEPARATELY, the proof REFUTES ITS OWN PARENT'S 'six terms': it records that T_4's bound-free differential 'vanishes ... identically' and that T_6 'currently returns 0 for A >= 5 atoms', so for 8 of the 12 tabulated atoms only three of the six terms contribute, while the parent proposition says the binding energy 'derives directly from the six terms'. The Open-questions section states this plainly and is exemplary; the parent does not.
